claims.text: The target eutectic high-entropy alloy has dual-phase lamellar colonies containing numerous internal boundaries.
Internal boundaries in the lamellar colonies are prone to microcrack initiation during room-temperature tensile deformation.
A trace Nb addition will segregate to the internal boundaries.
Nb segregation will trigger in situ formation of coherent nanoscale precipitates at internal boundaries.
The boundary precipitates will impede dislocation motion.
The boundary precipitates will reinforce or stabilize internal boundaries.
Stabilizing the internal boundaries will delay or prevent microcrack initiation.
The Nb-added alloy will have greater room-temperature tensile strength than the unmodified alloy through precipitation hardening.
The Nb-added alloy will have greater room-temperature tensile ductility than the unmodified alloy because of increased resistance to microcrack nucleation.
Tailored processing can preserve the inherited lamellar nature of an eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The beneficial Nb effect will occur only within a narrow optimized concentration range that produces coherent nanoscale precipitates.
Nb contents outside the beneficial range may cause deleterious phase embrittlement or loss of the lamellar morphology.
Internal phase boundaries can impede dislocation motion and act as strengthening agents in dual-phase eutectic high-entropy alloys.
